agent_notes: Physical constants sourced from Engineering Toolbox / Sera / Wikipedia; lamp PPE only partly stated (Nelson & Bugbee fluorescent 0.95). MET_CLASS, SALT_LOAD and most lamp numbers are our own choices with no stating page.

sources.quote: Water density at temperature 20 oC is 998.21 kg/m3

glass.note: inside the stated range; page says 'common' glass, does not say soda-lime

sources.quote: The bulk density of quartz sand/gravel is about 1.6 - 1.7 kg/l

sources.states: gravel dry 1680 kg/m3; sand dry 1555 kg/m3

substrate.note: dry bulk density; inside sera range

sources.states: porosity 0.36 to 0.43 for sandy soil; 0.20 for unsorted gravel
sources.quote: Typical bulk density of sandy soil is between 1.5 and 1.7 g/cm3. This calculates to a porosity between 0.43 and 0.36.

pore.note: ours is water held in gaps (kg/L) i.e. porosity x 1.0; 0.35 is within 20 % of the 0.36 low end. Aquarium gravel is sorted so 0.20 (unsorted, at depth) is not the right case

value.note: table row 'Water 20 oC' in Common Liquids; quote is the value cell only

tsand.note: terrestrial sand vs desert sand, broadband solar albedo not PAR; within 20 % (0.35 vs 0.40)

soil.note: Wikipedia Albedo gives bare soil 0.17 (opened) but that is generic bare soil, not dark planted-tank soil; no page stating aquarium-substrate PAR reflectance was found

white.note: no opened page states white aquarium sand or aragonite reflectance (desert sand 0.40 only); search snippets only, not opened

gravel.note: no opened page states natural gravel albedo; the other substrate colours (pea, clown, blue, onyx, black, coral, aragonite, clay, bark) are also our own estimates with no stating page

sources.quote: The best ceramic metal halide and fluorescent fixtures had efficiencies of 1.46 and 0.95 micromoles per joule, respectively.

t8.ppe.note: fixture-level (not bare lamp) best-in-test; 0.85 is within 20 % of 0.95; page does not say T8 specifically

sources.quote: The best ceramic metal halide and fluorescent fixtures had efficiencies of 1.46 and 0.95 micromoles per joule, respectively.

cfl.ppe.note: 0.8 is within 20 % of 0.95 (0.76 lower bound); page covers fluorescent fixtures generally, not CFL specifically; the full paper's T8 0.84 was not opened

t12.ppe.note: no page gives umol/J for T12. Hong Kong EMSD (opened, emsd.gov.hk .../lighting/tubes.html) gives T12 70 lm/W vs T8 80 lm/W, ratio 0.875; ours 0.7/0.85 = 0.82, a similar step down

led-bulb.ppe.note: no page gives umol/J for LED screw-in bulbs. EIA (opened, eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=15471) gives LED bulbs 'around 83 lumens per Watt' (2014), CFL 67, halogen 20, incandescent 16 lm/W; our 1.3 rests on ~90 lm/W over a lux factor, so it is lm/W-consistent but not a stated umol/J

halogen.ppe.note: no opened page gives halogen umol/J. EIA states halogen 'closer to 20 lumens per Watt' (lm/W only). A search snippet claimed a 20 W MR11 at 0.2 umol/s/W but that page was not opened

led-white.ppe.note: covered by reference/par-calibration-data.md (calibrated); Nelson & Bugbee best LED fixtures 1.66-1.70 umol/J appeared only in a search snippet, abstract opened states only fluorescent and ceramic MH figures in the quoted sentence

value.ours: messy 1.5, active 1.2, normal 1, sedentary 0.7, grazer 0.6, shrimp 0.5, shell 0.3, herp 0.4
value.note: Our own class multipliers after bioload rules of thumb (code comment). No page states per-class ratios; searches for published bioload ratios by activity class found nothing citable. Q10 = 2 in tempFactor is a separate constant, not sourced here

'half again' marine multiplier is a rule of thumb with no stating page; hobby sources found (search results only) say marine stocking is stricter (e.g. 1 inch per 5 gallons) but attribute it to filtration/reef complexity, not a 1.5x waste ratio

sources.states: 40 to 80 ppm nitrate (as NO3); 1 mg/L NO3-N = 4.4 ppm NO3
sources.quote: Most hobbyists are comfortable with anything from 40 to 80 ppm of nitrate

value.note: Code means mg/L as N (nitrate-N): 9 mg N/L x 4.4 = about 40 ppm NO3, the bottom of the stated 40-80 ppm range (NO3). The page also says hobbyist test kits read NO3, scientific studies NO3-N. Other hobby pages quote lower (20 ppm or less) for shrimp and sensitive fish
